routes.name: Standard Scramble (Appleton Pass / Boulder Lake approach)

claims.says: North / Northeast
Summit Mount Appleton via Appleton Pass and the South Ridge climbers' path
South Ridge scramble via Appleton Pass/Boulder Lake approach

contradictions.why: The route is described as the south ridge from Appleton Pass (south-southeast of the summit), but aspect says North / Northeast.

claims.says: late Jun-Sep
Full snow conditions; approach and summit slopes are typically still snowbound and outside the stated best-season window
this route is only climbed in the dry mid-July-September window
Late July through September for the most reliable snow-free conditions

contradictions.why: The season header opens in late June while the avalanche note says the route is only climbed mid-July to September and June is called fully snowbound.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Four fields (best_season, optimalWindow, approach_variants season, avalanche zone) start in mid/late July; the 'late Jun' in season is the outlier.

contradictions.fact: Direction of the Sol Duc River Trail

claims.says: Follow the Sol Duc River Trail west/north about 4.9 miles to the Appleton Pass Trail junction.
lng -123.750183 vs trailhead lng -123.835839 (junction is ~4 mi EAST/southeast of the trailhead)

contradictions.why: The schedule sends the party west/north, but the waypoints place the junction east-southeast of the trailhead (upriver).
contradictions.internal_resolution: Waypoint coordinates and the approach ('roughly 4.9 miles upriver') agree; 'west/north' is the outlier.

contradictions.why: dist_km (8 mi) is the one-way summit distance while the itinerary header shows 17 mi round trip; the Technical stats and header would show different distances for the same trip.
contradictions.internal_resolution: dist_km matches the one-way waypoint distance (8 mi); round trip is ~16-17 mi.

routes.name: Southwest Ridge via High Divide and the Catwalk

contradictions.fact: Route name referenced in prose (stale after rename)

claims.says: Southwest Ridge via High Divide and the Catwalk
Despite this route's name, there is no trail or known route connecting Hurricane Ridge to Cat Basin or Mount Carrie
Despite the route name, do not drive to Hurricane Ridge
despite what the route's name suggests

contradictions.why: The route is now named for the High Divide/Catwalk line, but three fields still warn that the route's NAME points to Hurricane Ridge, which it no longer does.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The current name is correct; the 'despite the route name' sentences in overview, waypoint directions and approach_variants are stale and should be reworded.

claims.says: One-way distance from the trailhead to the summit is roughly 13 miles.
11 (Heart Lake to summit and back)
Climb about 1.5 miles to the High Divide crest ... toward Cat Basin, about 3 miles
~1.5 mi class 3 ridge between Cat Peak and Carrie

contradictions.why: Itinerary gives 7 + 5.5 = ~12.5 mi one-way, pitch_detail legs sum to ~13-14 mi one-way (7 + 1.5 + 3 + 1.5 + <1), and approach says 13; the 11-mile summit day is short of what the pitch legs describe.

contradictions.fact: Boston Charlie's Camp: planned camp or emergency bivy

claims.says: treat it as an emergency bivy rather than a planned camp
Start early from Boston Charlie's Camp to ensure you cross the Catwalk in daylight
a party camped here can be on the summit early

contradictions.why: One field says not to plan to camp at Boston Charlie's while the pro tip and the camping card plan a start from it.

contradictions.fact: Boston Charlie's Camp elevation vs gain to summit

claims.says: the route gains around 2,000 ft in under a mile

contradictions.why: From 5,543 ft, 2,000 ft of gain would overshoot the 6,995 ft summit by ~550 ft; either the camp elevation or the gain figure is wrong.

claims.says: One-way distance from the trailhead to Boston Charlie's Camp/Cat Basin is roughly 13 miles

claims.field: waypoints[4] (High Divide / Cat Basin Trail junction).distMi

claims.says: Cat Basin lies just below the junction at roughly 5,042 ft

contradictions.why: The approach lumps Cat Basin with Boston Charlie's at ~13 miles, but the waypoints and camp card put Cat Basin at the 8.3-mile junction.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Waypoints and the bivy card agree Cat Basin is ~8.3 mi; the 13 mi applies only to Boston Charlie's.

claims.says: continue about 1 mile past the Deer Lake Trail junction, then roughly 6 more miles to Heart Lake

contradictions.why: Waypoints put the Deer Lake junction at 3.7 mi, so '+1 mi +6 mi' after it would put Heart Lake near 10.7 mi, not 7.85.

contradictions.fact: Where the party camps for the summit

claims.says: most parties camp at Heart Lake or Cat Basin and climb Carrie's summit as a long day from there
Camp near the toe of the Carrie Glacier
two days of approach through the Bailey Range to a high camp near the Carrie Glacier's toe

contradictions.why: The approach and approach_variants plan a summit day from Heart Lake/Cat Basin; the itinerary plans a second-night high camp at the glacier toe.

claims.says: roughly 31-mile round trip

contradictions.why: dist_km (13 mi) is roughly one-way while the header shows the 31-mile itinerary; the two distance displays disagree.

contradictions.fact: Boston Charlie's Camp elevation vs gain to summit

claims.says: the route gains around 2,000 ft in under a mile

contradictions.why: From 5,543 ft, 2,000 ft of gain overshoots the 6,995 ft summit by ~550 ft.

claims.says: head northeast down the Carrie Glacier (rope up and put on crampons here ...), circle around to the north of Fairchild, and climb its Southwest Ridge
reclimb the Carrie Glacier roped up with crampons to Mount Carrie's summit
Fairchild Glacier crossing
Aim to reach the upper Fairchild Glacier at roughly 6,700 ft
the line drops from Mount Carrie onto the Fairchild Glacier

contradictions.why: Approach and descent_text put the route on the Carrie Glacier (and a Southwest Ridge finish after circling north), while waypoints, approach_variants and crevasses put it on the Fairchild Glacier's snow ridge to the summit ridge.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Waypoints (with directions), approach_variants and crevasses agree on the Fairchild Glacier line; approach/descent_text 'Carrie Glacier' is the outlier.

claims.says: leads up Carrie's ridge and upper flanks to its summit. The route to Fairchild starts from Mount Carrie's summit
Mount Carrie ridge/glacier gain, elev 6995

contradictions.why: The route crosses Mount Carrie's 6,995 ft summit, so the route's high point is 6,995 ft, not 6,900.

claims.says: Climb roughly 1,700 ft southeast from Boston Charlie's onto Mount Carrie (6,995 ft)
the route gains around 2,000 ft in under a mile

contradictions.why: Waypoint puts the camp at 5,300 ft (1,700 ft below Carrie) while the camping card says 5,543 ft and 2,000 ft of gain, which cannot both hold.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The waypoint elevation and its 1,700 ft figure are self-consistent; the bivy card is the outlier.

claims.says: consistent with the 12-hour summit-day timing estimate starting from high camp

contradictions.why: Partner requirements cite a 12-hour summit day that no timing field states.
contradictions.internal_resolution: timing and itinerary both say 10 hours.

claims.says: Mid-July through early September
Late July through September - the short window when the Bailey Range is reliably snow-free enough
Late July to mid-September
Mid-July through mid-August is the reported sweet spot

contradictions.why: The best window starts mid-July and ends early September in one field but starts late July and runs through September in another.

claims.says: commonly via Appleton Pass, Cat Basin, and Ferry Basin/Eleven Bull Basin
follow the Sol Duc River Trail ... to Heart Lake (7.85 mi) and the High Divide/Bailey Range junction
climb through subalpine meadows to the High Divide/Heart Lake area

contradictions.why: Beta names Appleton Pass (and Ferry Basin) as the usual approach, while every other field routes via Heart Lake/High Divide to Eleven Bull Basin; Ferry Basin lies beyond the peak.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Approach, waypoints, itinerary, timing and approach_variants all use Heart Lake/High Divide; beta is the outlier.

claims.says: Most parties are back at camp by early-to-mid afternoon.
11:00 AM Back at Eleven Bull Basin camp

contradictions.why: The note and the schedule on the same day disagree about when the party is back at camp.

claims.says: No rappel/descent beta was found for this route.
a single rappel from the summit block back down to the notch/col it rises from

contradictions.why: The rope note says no rappel beta exists while descent_text and rappels describe a specific single rappel.

contradictions.fact: Timing of the Flypaper Pass snow finger

claims.says: this section is best done in spring or early summer before it melts out
the finger typically melts out by late summer, so climb it early season
Core of the best-season window - glacier and spire typically most snow-free and stable
Jul-Sep

contradictions.why: Approach and waypoint say to climb in spring/early summer before the finger melts, while the season is Jul-Sep with August as optimal.

claims.says: roughly 38-mile round trip
the ~38-mile round-trip distance

contradictions.why: dist_km is 19.5 mi (one-way) while the header and prose give a 38-mile round trip.

claims.says: The same pass is reached from the Dosewallips on the east side, which is the shorter approach to the Anderson massif if that road is open
the Dosewallips River Road (FR-2610) ... has been closed to vehicles at a washout since 2002

contradictions.why: The camping card treats the Dosewallips road as possibly open, while the route itself is built on the road having been closed since 2002.

contradictions.fact: Descent line off the summit block

claims.says: reverse the same line to descend
do NOT reverse the ascent gully — parties consistently and strongly recommend downclimbing the left (west) side of the summit block/notch instead
the same line the descent explicitly avoids downclimbing

contradictions.why: The itinerary says to descend the ascent line, while descent_text and climbing_route say not to downclimb the ascent gully.
contradictions.internal_resolution: descent_text and climbing_route agree on descending the west side; the itinerary note is the outlier.

claims.says: the Switchback trail gains close to 1,000 ft in under a mile
about 700 ft in 0.6 mile
gains about 700-800 ft in 0.6 mi

contradictions.why: The camp card still gives ~1,000 ft for the Switchback Trail after the other fields were set to 700-800 ft.
contradictions.internal_resolution: beta and approach agree on 700-800 ft in 0.6 mi.

contradictions.fact: Time to the base of the scramble

claims.says: Roughly 2-3 hours from the Hurricane Ridge area to the base of the summit scramble
9:00 AM Summit (6,454 ft) after a 7:00 AM start

contradictions.why: The schedule reaches the summit 2 hours after leaving the lot, while partner requirements say 2-3 hours just to the base of the scramble.

contradictions.fact: Whether the crux step is roped

claims.says: many parties spot or rope this step
There is no roped climbing on the standard route
No technical rock pro on the standard line

contradictions.why: The crux waypoint says many parties rope the step while beta says there is no roped climbing.

contradictions.fact: Where the summit-day gear cache is

claims.says: Cache tents/sleeping gear in the meadow southeast of Barnes
Bear Pass ... the ground drops into a flat meadow ... contour southeast over scree ... until you are southwest of the summit
lat 47.7987, lng -123.5863 (northwest of the summit)

contradictions.why: The camp meadow is below Bear Pass, northwest of the peak, from which the route contours southeast; the schedule places it southeast of Barnes.

claims.says: June-August is the most reliable weather window overall
risky — interior basin typically still snowbound; not considered in season
Jul-Sep

contradictions.why: Climate calls June part of the most reliable window while the seasonal guidance calls June risky and out of season.

claims.says: Sol Duc to High Divide / Cat Basin

contradictions.why: Day 1 ends at Cat Basin after 7.5 miles, but Heart Lake, which comes before Cat Basin, is at 7.85 miles.

claims.says: set a firm early-afternoon turnaround time on summit day
4:00-5:00 AM Alpine start recommended
~4:00 PM Summit (6,182 ft) — Reference party topped out at 4:20 PM after a 9 AM start

contradictions.why: The schedule pairs a 4-5 AM start with a ~4 PM summit carried over from a 9 AM start, which also overruns the stated early-afternoon turnaround.
contradictions.internal_resolution: With the recommended 4-5 AM start and the reference party's ~7.3 hr to the summit, the summit would be ~11:30 AM-12:30 PM; the ~4:00 PM time is stale.

claims.says: this is 28.4 miles from Whiskey Bend up the Elwha
No mileage is quoted for this side because published figures assume Whiskey Bend is drivable

contradictions.why: The camp card quotes a mileage for the Elwha side that the approach variant says is deliberately not quoted.

claims.says: reached via 4.4 mi of narrow gravel Whiskey Bend Road, which washes out and closes periodically
Closed to vehicles at Madison Falls due to washout
adds roughly 7 miles each way of road walking or biking just to reach the Whiskey Bend trailhead

contradictions.why: The trailhead note implies the trailhead is reached by driving Whiskey Bend Road, while road, access and approach say it has been closed to vehicles since 2017.
contradictions.internal_resolution: road, access.closures, approach and trailheadDirection agree it is closed; the waypoint note is the outlier.

contradictions.fact: Elwha Snowfinger exit: planned route or closed

claims.says: From Dodwell-Rixon Pass, descend the Elwha Snowfinger gully, now largely melted out
The Elwha Snowfinger exit is also effectively closed by natural melt-out.
Rangers now commonly route parties back north to the Ferry-Pulitzer col and out via Dodger Point instead
Elwha Snowfinger exit ... no longer reliably passable (2023-2025 reports) -- do not rely on it

contradictions.why: The trip plan exits down the Snowfinger, which access calls effectively closed and descent says rangers now route around via Dodger Point.

contradictions.fact: Ascent vs descent slope on Ferry

claims.says: South Slopes (Bailey Range)
do Mount Ferry as a side excursion via the southeast ridge (loose 'dagger' scree), descending the easier south slope
The standard way down reverses the ascent scree/talus slope on the peak's southeast side, which parties describe as distinctly easier than the way up
Broad bench and scree slope east of the summit

contradictions.why: The itinerary climbs the SE ridge and descends a different, easier south slope; descent_text says the descent reverses the ascent slope yet is easier than the way up; the route is named for the south slopes but climbs the east bench.

claims.says: steep heather benches with class 3-4 moves
Exposed Class 3 to 4 moves on the catwalks
exposed Class 2-3 scrambling while carrying a full overnight pack

contradictions.why: Partner requirements ask only for Class 2-3 skill, while the approach the party must cross includes Class 3-4 moves.

claims.says: the North Fork itself right at this camp ... The peak rises about 3,800 ft above the river

claims.field: waypoints[5] (North Fork Quinault River Ford / Leave Trail).elev

claims.says: climb roughly 3,800-4,000 ft up the 'hidden gully' system

contradictions.why: The same ford/camp is at 1,050 ft in the waypoint and 2,021 ft on the camp card, and 3,800-4,000 ft of climbing to the 5,401 ft summit puts the river near 1,400-1,600 ft, matching neither.

claims.says: Multi-day approach (2+ days) via the southern Olympic trail network to a high camp
Day 1: 12 miles to a riverside camp; Day 2: summit and full hike-out
Alpine start from high camp

contradictions.why: The itinerary is a one-day approach to a river-level camp and a 2-day trip; partner requirements and timing describe a 2+ day approach to a high camp.

contradictions.fact: When camp is broken on summit day

claims.says: Break camp, cross river
Retrace the route back down to camp, then break camp and hike the full ~12 miles back

contradictions.why: The schedule breaks camp before dawn, while the note breaks camp after returning from the summit.

contradictions.fact: Ridge crossed from the Quinault side

claims.says: via the North Fork Quinault River Trail ... and over the Christie-Noyes ridge
a scree traverse to the Noyes/Seattle notch
From a Seattle Basin camp, cross the head of Seattle Creek and climb to the saddle just east of Noyes

contradictions.why: The approach crosses a Christie-Noyes ridge, while the itinerary and base-finding go from Seattle Basin through the Noyes/Seattle notch.

contradictions.fact: Date of the Olympic Hot Springs Road washout

claims.says: the end of vehicle access since November 2017 flood damage
As of the 2024 Olympic Hot Springs Road washout

contradictions.why: Two fields give different years for the washout that closed the road.
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach and road.driveNote ('closed for roughly a decade') agree on 2017; the itinerary's 2024 is the outlier.

claims.says: Multi-day approach (commonly 2+ days each way)
Day 4: one 16.8-mile hike-out day

contradictions.why: Partner requirements say 2+ days each way, while the itinerary walks out in a single day.

contradictions.fact: Date of the Elwha road washout

claims.says: Since the 2024 Elwha road washout
closed to vehicles beyond Madison Falls since November 2017 flood damage
since November 2017 flood damage

contradictions.why: The pro tip gives 2024 for the washout; approach and access say November 2017.
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach and access.closures agree on 2017; the pro tip is the outlier.

contradictions.fact: Height of the scramble above the tarn

claims.says: sidehill the faint Mount Olson Way Trail ... to a small tarn at the base of the peak, then scramble roughly 1,000 ft up steep meadow and heather
A boulder-field tarn at about 5,100 ft below the summit block

contradictions.why: A tarn at 5,100 ft is only ~190 ft below the 5,289 ft summit, so a 1,000 ft scramble from the tarn to the top cannot both be true.

claims.says: dry beyond Camp Bellevue, so ... carrying/caching all water for the final push
Boulder-field tarn just below the summit block is the last water
A boulder-field tarn at about 5,100 ft below the summit block is the last water

contradictions.why: The itinerary says the route is dry past Camp Bellevue, while the waypoint and approach variant name a tarn below the summit as the last water.
